overall: Atlanta reached a running maximum of 91.4°F by around 16:19 ET, then experienced a sharp post-storm temperature drop to 80.6°F by 17:52 — a classic convective cooling signature consistent with the active severe thunderstorm watch and warnings in effect through 11 PM EDT. The day ran hotter than models anticipated, with dewpoints in the low-to-mid 70s fueling an unusually warm airmass before thunderstorm outflow drove the evening collapse. With current temp at 82.4°F as of 19:49 and ongoing storm activity, temperatures will not recover to challenge the afternoon peak.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models (ECMWF 87.5°F, HRRR 90.1°F, NBM 86.8°F) underestimated today's observed high by 1.3–4.6°F; even the warmest model (HRRR) fell short of the actual running max. The META bucket model was directionally correct in concentrating mass at 90–93°F, though the INTRADAY model's 96.8% concentration at 90–91°F slightly undershot the realized 91.4°F peak.
max_temp_prediction: The daily TMAX is effectively locked in at 91.4°F — the give-up classifier fired at hour 14.67 (when running max was 89.6°F, prob=91%), the hour of max was confirmed at 16:19 ET over 3.5 hours ago, and post-storm outflow has already driven temperatures down to 82.4°F with severe thunderstorms still ongoing. There is virtually no meteorological pathway for temperatures to rebound above 91.4°F at this hour. Confidence is extremely high that 91.4°F is the final TMAX.
